# Without the hooks nothing refreshes the plaintext after a pull, so the next
# seal used to write the old plaintext straight back over the pulled object.
# git remembers where the worktree came from (ORIG_HEAD, the reflog), which is
# enough to see that the plaintext is the old version and not an edit.

sesam-repo admin base.txt changed.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'
exec git checkout master

# A fast-forward pull with the hooks out of the way.
exec sesam hook uninstall
exec git merge topic
stdout 'Fast-forward'
exec cat s
stdout 'BASE'

# Status knows the plaintext lags behind, and seal leaves the object alone.
exec sesam status
stdout 'S s'
stdout '1 stale'
exec sesam seal
stderr 'not sealed - the object is newer than the plaintext'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'

# Reveal catches up; nothing is left to say afterwards.
exec sesam reveal
exec cat s
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam status
stdout 'everything in sync'

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- changed.txt --
CHANGED
